Q1: Silver exhibits known significant hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental hazards (ENV), and organ/systemic hazards (OGN). It also shows an expanded perspective of potential hazards (Tier 2) for endocrine disruption (EDC) and dermal/eye hazards (SKN), based on current scientific data beyond the GHS. Conversely, direct studies support a favorable safety profile (Tier 3) for inhalation (IHL) and oral (ORL) hazards.
Q2: Silver is identified on several lists of concern, including the TEDX list, which indicates it as a potential endocrine disruptor. Additionally, it is subject to regulation under the EPA's Drinking Water Standard due to its classification as a drinking water contaminant.
Q3: Silver is exceptionally well-characterized, with over 616,000 scientific literature references, far exceeding the median for our dataset of chemicals. Its simple molecular formula (Ag), classification as an element, and lack of any data-deficient (Tier 4) hazard categories further confirm its extensive study and a complete understanding of its hazard profile.
